lead.headline: Tokenized equity perps push RWA monthly volume to $470B as S&P launches blockchain index
lead.tldr: Institutional infrastructure for crypto-native assets is hardening faster than the regulatory framework around them, creating a widening execution gap between what markets can build and what compliance will allow.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, here is what moved in Web3 over the last 24 hours and why the tension between market infrastructure and regulatory clarity is becoming the defining trade for H2 2024.

top_signals.title: Tokenized equity perps drive RWA trading boom to $470 billion monthly volume
top_signals.summary: Real World Asset (RWA) trading has experienced a massive surge, reaching $470 billion in monthly volume. This growth is primarily driven by the popularity of tokenized equity perpetuals over tokenized commodities.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The $470 billion monthly volume in tokenized equity perps versus commodities signals that crypto-native capital prefers synthetic exposure to familiar equities over novel on-chain real assets, which constrains the RWA thesis to a derivatives story rather than an ownership revolution.

top_signals.title: AFX protocol reportedly loses $24M in bridge exploit33m
top_signals.summary: The AFX protocol has reportedly suffered a bridge exploit resulting in a loss of approximately $24 million. The incident highlights ongoing vulnerabilities in cross-chain bridge infrastructure.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The $24 million bridge exploit at AFX protocol reinforces that cross-chain infrastructure remains the single highest-beta liability in any DeFi underwriting, and we continue to price bridge risk at multiples above base-layer risk.

top_signals.title: Bipartisan support 'critical' as Democrats push back on GOP crypto bill on ethics grounds
top_signals.summary: The Clarity Act, a GOP-led crypto bill, is facing opposition from Democrats on ethics grounds despite support from the crypto industry. The divide highlights significant political tension between lawmakers and the banking sector regarding the regulation of digital assets.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Democratic pushback on the Clarity Act on ethics grounds rather than policy substance suggests the bill's path to passage is narrower than industry pricing implies, and bipartisan support may require stripping provisions that make the bill valuable to crypto issuers in the first place.

top_signals.title: S&P launches blockchain fundamentals index for digital assets 11m
top_signals.summary: S&P Dow Jones Indices has launched a new blockchain fundamentals index designed to track the performance of digital assets based on network activity and usage. This move signals increased institutional validation and the creation of standardized benchmarks for the crypto market.
top_signals.why_it_matters: S&P Dow Jones launching a blockchain fundamentals index creates the data infrastructure for institutional mandates and passive flows, which historically precedes ETF approvals and pension board discussions by 18-24 months.

top_signals.title: SEC’s Peirce Warns Onchain Lending May Trigger Securities Laws
top_signals.summary: SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce has warned that certain onchain lending products and crypto vaults may be classified as securities under U.S. law. She urged developers to evaluate their compliance obligations to avoid potential regulatory enforcement.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Peirce's warning that onchain lending products may trigger securities laws is notable precisely because she is the SEC's most crypto-friendly commissioner, meaning this is the outer bound of regulatory accommodation and anything stricter will come from her colleagues.

deals.summary: Benchmark has raised its price target for Hut 8 by 18%, viewing the company as a potential 'power-first data center REIT.' This outlook suggests a significant upside for the stock, which has already seen substantial growth year-to-date.

on_the_radar.title: BitGo, OTC Markets plan tokenized securities access for broker-dealers43m
on_the_radar.summary: BitGo and OTC Markets are collaborating to provide broker-dealers with access to tokenized securities. This initiative aims to bridge traditional finance and digital assets by streamlining the trading and settlement of tokenized assets.

on_the_radar.title: Zilliqa halts native transactions over bug in its Ledger app dating to 2019
on_the_radar.summary: Zilliqa has halted native transactions following the discovery of a critical bug in its Ledger app. The vulnerability, which dates back to 2019, reportedly exposed users' private keys through on-chain signatures.

on_the_radar.title: TRON Included in S&P Pantera Digital Asset Index as Institutional Benchmarking Expands to Blockchain Networks
on_the_radar.summary: TRON has been added to the S&P Pantera Digital Asset Index, marking a significant step in institutional benchmarking for blockchain networks. This inclusion reflects growing institutional adoption and the integration of TRON into professional investment frameworks.

on_the_radar.title: Clarity Act’s impact on Circle could be negative over the long term, Mizuho says
on_the_radar.summary: Mizuho analysts suggest that the Clarity Act legislation could have a negative long-term impact on Circle. The act is moving closer to becoming law following the release of the latest text by Republicans.

on_the_radar.title: Kraken parent Payward partners with GTN to scale xStocks internationally, beyond US equities
on_the_radar.summary: Payward, the parent company of Kraken, has partnered with GTN to expand xStocks internationally. The initiative focuses on tokenizing equities, starting with Hong Kong and expanding into the UK, Europe, and South Korea.

on_the_radar.title: Digital Chamber sues Illinois officials over new state 0.2% crypto tax1h, Digital Chamber sues Illinois officials over new state 0.2% crypto tax
on_the_radar.summary: The Digital Chamber has filed a lawsuit against Illinois officials challenging a new 0.2% state tax on cryptocurrency transactions. The organization argues that the tax is unconstitutional and creates an undue burden on digital asset users.

on_the_radar.title: Franklin Templeton calls agentic AI next ‘killer’ use case for blockchain35m
on_the_radar.summary: Franklin Templeton identifies agentic AI as the next major catalyst for blockchain adoption. The firm suggests that AI agents capable of autonomous financial decision-making will drive significant utility and demand for on-chain infrastructure.

on_the_radar.title: Bitcoin ETFs Add $930M Inflows Over Six-Day Streak
on_the_radar.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs experienced a six-day streak of inflows, totaling $930 million. The most recent Tuesday saw an addition of $203.1 million as Bitcoin's price briefly surpassed $66,700.

worth_a_read.title: Revolut hits $115bn valuation in employee share sale, reports say
worth_a_read.note: Revolut's $115 billion employee share sale valuation provides a private-market comp for fintech-crypto hybrid business models and suggests secondary market liquidity for late-stage European tech is deeper than commonly assumed.

linkedin_post:
S&P Dow Jones now runs a blockchain fundamentals index. Not a price index—network activity, usage, on-chain metrics. That distinction matters. Price indices let traders bet. Fundamentals indices let allocators justify. The second audience has longer lockups and harder due diligence standards. We have been waiting for this infrastructure layer to arrive before calling institutional adoption anything more than anecdotal.

The timing is not accidental. Tokenized equity perpetuals just drove RWA volume to $470 billion monthly. That number is almost entirely derivatives, not ownership. Markets want exposure, not custody. S&P's index will track the rails that enable both, which means the benchmarkers are betting the infrastructure outlasts the regulatory ambiguity.

That ambiguity is sharpening. Hester Peirce, the SEC's most sympathetic voice to crypto, just warned that onchain lending products may be securities. If that is the friendly position, the unfriendly one is easy to imagine. The Clarity Act, meanwhile, faces Democratic opposition on ethics grounds—not policy, ethics. The bill may pass in name and be hollowed in substance.

What we underwrite here: the gap between what S&P can index and what the SEC will permit is where the next 12 months of value creation and destruction will concentrate. The test is whether any tokenized equity perpetual platform can secure a broker-dealer framework before the enforcement window closes. We do not know the answer. We know the window is narrow.
